speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This virus has affected not only China but many countries worldwide and cases are still growing daily with no signs of abating yet.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have, therefore, put in place pre-emptive measures to protect the public health.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is heartening to know that China is doing all they can to contain the spread of the virus, and we have witnessed their decisive actions to put in place strong measures, such as travel restrictions for their own residents, cancellation of outbound tour groups, and bringing back residents from overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We wish China well in their efforts to combat this virus and we have every confidence that China and other countries, including us here in Singapore, will work together and complement one another to win this battle internationally.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is not just a problem for China but for the world.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have to work together and collaborate with one another.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: More details about the package will be provided later.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I can understand why Singaporeans are concerned as there are many unknowns about the virus: how it will develop and how long this will last.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Beyond health, businesses would also have concerns as many have been affected by our prevention and containment measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister Lawrence Wong, my co-chair of the Taskforce, will provide more details on the efforts of the various Government agencies and how we are working together with all the stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As the situation unfolds, we will share as much information as possible and as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While we cannot be complacent, I am confident we will overcome this challenge as we have in the past if we work together.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have been preparing for this, we are anticipating scenarios ahead, taking decisive actions as the situation evolves and we will do our best to keep Singapore and Singaporeans safe.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The situation in China and globally is still developing rapidly even as we speak and we still have very limited knowledge of the virus as scientists all over the world are racing against time to understand this virus better.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The virus was first detected in Wuhan in December 2019, although it may well have existed earlier while remaining undetected.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On 31 December, the WHO was first informed of a cluster of pneumonia cases of unknown cause detected in Wuhan.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Soon after, on 2 January, the Ministry of Health (MOH) alerted our medical professionals and effected temperature screening for all flights arriving from Wuhan at our airport.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We anticipated that we would need a whole-of-Government effort to respond swiftly to this threat when it arrives in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We had to take precautions and coordinate plans across Government agencies to fight this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In fact, the following day, after we had set up the Taskforce, we saw the first local imported case.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Wuhan and additional cities in Hubei were then locked down by the Chinese government.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: By this time, we had already issued travel advisories for Wuhan and extended our temperature screening at the airport to all incoming flights from China.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The infection continued to spread at a rapid pace, reaching several foreign countries and all provinces of China by 29 January 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Twenty-three countries have also reported a total of 146 confirmed cases and one death.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Forty-three recently admitted suspect cases are pending test results while 240 suspect cases were tested and cleared.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: All of the confirmed cases are being treated in isolation rooms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Overall, the conditions of most of our confirmed cases are improving.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To date, there is no evidence of local community transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, we should not be complacent and we must be prepared for this scenario.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This virus comes from the family of coronavirus, which includes other viruses, such as the Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS) and severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), as well as the milder variants causing the common cold.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The medical consensus at this moment is that the novel coronavirus is more transmissible but appears less deadly than SARS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Available evidence suggests that the rate of human-to-human transmission of this virus appears to be higher than that of SARS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For now, the evidence also suggests that transmission is mostly via droplets.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: What this means is that the virus is carried within droplets emitted from an infected person over a short distance, such as when the person coughs or sneezes.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If these droplets come into contact with the eyes, nose or mouth of an individual, directly or indirectly through hands that have come into contact with these droplets, the individual may become infected.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To clarify, there is no evidence currently to suggest that the virus is airborne.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There are other viruses, such as chickenpox, which can easily be transported via air currents and do not require droplets to contact the eyes, nose or mouth.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The novel coronavirus is not in this category of viruses.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The novel coronavirus could also transmit through surface contact.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: When a person sneezes or coughs, the droplets fall onto the surfaces of tables and chairs, for example, and the virus may remain alive for up to a few days.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: When someone else touches the surfaces of these tables and chairs, the virus can be transferred to his hand and if he then rubs his eyes or nose without washing his hands, he may become infected.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is also why we only quarantine the close contacts of confirmed cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For more transient contacts, such as individuals that the confirmed cases may have walked past in malls or hotels, the risk of transmission is low.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, this form of transmission may be uncommon and has so far involved isolated cases only.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At this point, the evidence still points towards higher transmissibility when the person is displaying symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As such, medical professionals both overseas and in Singapore have advised that the most effective way that we can protect ourselves is to practise good personal hygiene.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We should regularly wash our hands with soap and water, and avoid touching our face with our hands.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These may sound simple, but are actually very difficult to do because all of us touch our face all the time.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even in a meeting that we had with the Multi-Ministry Taskforce while I was speaking, I was touching my face until Minister Lawrence Wong nudged me with his elbow and said, "Stop touching your face".

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: So, it is simple but effective in preventing all kinds of infection.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Potential infection from asymptomatic persons, in fact, is less likely to be from coughing or sneezing directly because they do not have symptoms, such as sneezing or coughing, but more likely by touching contaminated surfaces, for which masks offer no protection.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Wearing a mask when we are well often give us a false sense of security instead and we are more likely to touch our faces when we constantly adjust our masks, which is one way the disease spreads.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the same time, we need to protect others – our loved ones, friends, colleagues and fellow Singaporeans that we come into contact with.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If we are sick, we should rest and recover at home as far as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If we do need to go out to see a doctor, for example, we should wear a surgical mask to protect others.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: So, this is when a mask is needed – when we are unwell and have to go out.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The current approach is to provide good supportive care for the patients to reduce complications and to allow time for the patient to recover.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The majority of the deaths are among those with underlying medical conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But we are still at the initial stages of the outbreak and the actual severity can only be assessed properly in time to come.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Regardless, the Government’s response has been, and will continue to be swift and decisive, to contain the spread of the virus here.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have been preparing for the possibility of an infectious disease outbreak like this one since SARS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have been building capacity and capability in addressing infectious diseases, such as SARS, MERS, H1N1, and more recently Zika and Monkey Pox.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We had strengthened our epidemiological surveillance and containment capabilities and our agencies hold regular emergency preparedness exercises to keep themselves operationally ready.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In addition, we have set up the National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID), a purpose-built facility to strengthen our ability to manage the outbreak of infectious diseases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is benchmarked to international standards and best practices for treatment and safety.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In April 2018, a Joint External Evaluation by the WHO experts stated that Singapore had demonstrated strong leadership and high capacity to detect and respond to potential public health emergencies.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We had followed the situation in Wuhan closely since December 2019 and we had responded rapidly, putting in place a series of measures to reduce the risk of import and spread of the virus since early January 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include the implementation of temperature screening at the airport and we also alerted all our medical practitioners to be vigilant.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Once we saw a significant increase in confirmed cases in Wuhan, I decided that it was necessary to set up a Multi-Ministry Taskforce.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I asked Minister Lawrence Wong to co-chair this, and invited the Deputy Prime Minister as our advisor.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Taskforce is to plan and coordinate whole-of-Government efforts so that we can mount a national response quickly and effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Representatives from the Ministries of Home Affairs, Social and Family Development, Transport, Education, Manpower, Trade and Industry, Communications and Information, the Environment and Water Resources, and the Labour Movement are all involved.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The list is very long, but it is a reflection of the multi-agency coordination that is required.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We had set up multiple lines of defence to reduce the risk of imported cases and local community transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have been stepping up our posture and efforts at each line of defence.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, we have measures that serve to prevent further importation of the virus into our shores.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These include temperature and health screening at all checkpoints, land, sea and air, as well as international travel controls.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Second, we have measures that help us to detect and contain the virus and prevent it from spreading further.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have good surveillance systems to identify cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our healthcare providers, especially our polyclinics and general practitioners, are right at the frontline.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They are on heightened alert and stand ready to deal with cases as they emerge.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Third, and perhaps most importantly, all of us must play our part and exercise social responsibility, to prevent or stem any possible spread of the coronavirus in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We should also be considerate for others around us and lend a hand as a community to support one another and stay united.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: None of these measures on their own is fool-proof.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But when taken together, they will improve our resilience and ability to respond to this disease.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister Wong will touch on the other measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our healthcare providers play a key role in the detection and isolation of suspected and confirmed cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our frontline doctors, polyclinics, general practitioners (GPs) and Emergency Department doctors are on high alert for persons with travel history and respiratory symptoms, such as fever and cough.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Such persons will be assessed, isolated and tested for the novel coronavirus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will also test samples from our influenza surveillance systems and hospitalised pneumonia cases for novel coronavirus to pick up unlinked cases, if any.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many of them stayed mostly at their hotels or with their family in their family's homes, and did not move around extensively.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, some of them did visit our tourism sites, such as Gardens by the Bay and Orchard Road, where any interactions would have been transient.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The confirmed cases are being treated at various hospitals and their conditions are stable and most of them are improving.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: With each confirmed case, we will conduct contact tracing.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will check on the health of these contacts and if they are unwell with fever, cough or other respiratory symptoms, they will be classified as suspected cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will arrange for them to go to hospitals via a dedicated ambulance for isolation and testing.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For contacts that are well, we adopt a risk-based approach.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The detection and management of suspect cases and proper care and isolation of these confirmed cases would not have been possible without our healthcare providers and professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They are our key partners in this war against the novel coronavirus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our polyclinics and GP partners play an important role in identifying and notifying MOH of any cases that meet the case definition so that they can be followed up.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Dr Lam Pin Min and I recently met a group of GPs, including representatives from the Singapore Medical Association (SMA) and the College of Family Physicians Singapore (CFPS), to hear their feedback and see how we can support them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our hospitals will similarly isolate any individuals that present themselves at the emergency department who meet the case definition and test them to determine whether they are infected with the novel coronavirus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They have worked tirelessly over the last few weeks, missing their holidays or reunion dinners.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They work very hard to keep Singaporeans and Singapore safe.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Their families may also need to take over caregiving duties at home or make alternative arrangements as these healthcare workers work overtime to manage the cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Dr Margaret Soon, the Director of Nursing at NCID.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: She was a veteran from SARS, and an Infection Control Nurse.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Dr Soon immediately rose to the occasion when we activated NCID.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: She led her team to prepare the isolation rooms, held townhalls to update the NCID nurses and ensured that her nurses had adequate essential supplies, such as protective gowns and masks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Throughout this period, she was out of the house before sunrise and mostly back only after her family had gone to asleep.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: She had to cancel a family trip during the Chinese New Year period, but her family understood and was supportive.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This included her daughter, whom she was pregnant with during SARS.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Stories of such dedication like Dr Soon's abound in our healthcare community.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I would also like to emphasise that there is no need to avoid our healthcare workers during this time.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have instituted strict safety policies and procedures in our hospitals and other healthcare providers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, healthcare workers managing cases are required to don personal protective equipment and this ensures that they are protected from the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Instead, let us stand together, stand behind them and support them in this period.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They may be our friends and family, or even strangers that we meet on the streets or public transport.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A smile, a kind word or an encouraging message goes a long way towards helping them keep their spirits up and know that we are behind them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am also very encouraged by our various community-led efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: For example, Akram Hanif and his youth volunteers have been engaging a group of about 45 young adolescents and youths at Marsiling Community Centre/Club (CC) to instil in them good values and character.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Akram had organised the kids to draw a banner to thank our frontline medical staff from Tan Tock Seng Hospital and encourage them to press on.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are not sure how long this virus will turn out.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Therefore, we must stand ready to respond to new developments as the situation evolves.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There remain risks ahead and we are preparing for the various contingencies.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We may need to roll out additional measures to prevent the importation and to contain the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The decision to do so would again not be an easy one.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have to do what is necessary to protect the health and safety of our people and those who travel to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Despite our best efforts, this is a possibility that we must be ready for.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The key to managing this is quick detection and limiting further spread, which calls on social responsibility from all of us.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: If the infected Singaporean wears a mask to protect others and promptly sees a doctor and gets triaged for testing, the risk of further spread can be greatly reduced.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even if there is spread, quick action will help to limit its extent.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Once tested positive, the Government will contact-trace quickly, helping to reduce further spread to their close contacts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And we have to assess what best to do, depending on how the virus mutates.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It may also become less infectious on the other hand and less severe, but it is a scenario that we worry about when it comes.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On the healthcare front, we are stepping up preparations for these potential scenarios.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have also been increasing our testing capacity, to enable us to more quickly to confirm suspect cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our early intervention efforts have helped to contain the spread so far, but while we hope for the best, we must plan for the worst.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I am very heartened by the many examples of volunteers stepping forward to support our efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I have elaborated on the public health measures that we have put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Minister Lawrence Wong will elaborate on the other measures.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I would also like to acknowledge once again our healthcare workers on the frontlines and commend them for their bravery and selflessness.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Let us stand together and show our support for them.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We understand that Singaporeans may feel anxious, given the many unknowns about the novel coronavirus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Here, I want to reiterate the Government's firm commitment that we will spare no efforts in protecting our people.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will act swiftly and share information on the novel coronavirus openly and as soon as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have overcome several challenges as a nation in the past – SARS, H1N1 and Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In the face of this novel coronavirus, we have built up our defences, our capabilities and we are stronger and more prepared.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: While we cannot be complacent, we must remain calm and confident.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is a fight that calls on every individual to do our part.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are confident that we can manage and overcome this challenge as a nation and emerge stronger together.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Minister for National Development will be making a related Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will allow Members to raise points of clarification on both Statements after this Statement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will now elaborate on the other aspects of the work of the Multi-Ministry Taskforce.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Taskforce was formed just about two weeks ago, and we have been meeting almost daily since then to deal with a very fast moving and constantly changing situation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The novel coronavirus is a new virus, and medical experts everywhere are rushing to understand more about how it spreads, how severe it is and how it can be treated.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we constantly update our risk assessments based on the latest information and expert advice.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also look ahead to anticipate as best as we can how the situation will evolve and prepare for the possibility that things can worsen.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why over the past week alone, we have had to adjust and update our measures several times.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We owe it to every Singaporean to do our very best to protect all of us from the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, in all that we do, the overall health and well-being of Singaporeans have been and will be our top priority.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Minister Gan Kim Yong highlighted earlier, the measures we put in place are part of a broader system with multiple lines of defence.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our first line of defence against an infectious disease that occurs outside of Singapore is to put in place controls at the border to limit the spread of the virus and the number of imported cases here.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The world is more connected than before, with more people flying around and travelling than ever.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we have to be extra vigilant on this front because Singapore is an international travel hub, with more than 68 million people using our airport last year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, a virus that comes through our airport will not only impact Singapore, but it can also easily spread through us to other countries in the region.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have to be extra vigilant.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To protect against such an infectious disease outbreak when it happens outside of Singapore, we have a series of drawer plans and measures at the border.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They range from the screening of in-bound travellers, to placing high-risk travellers into quarantine, as well as restricting travel for those who have recently been to high-risk countries.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And then, depending on the nature of the outbreak, we will assess the risks and put in place the appropriate measures.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is the approach the Taskforce has taken in dealing with this virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We first implemented temperature screening at Changi Airport for flights from Wuhan.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And then, we expanded the screening to all flights from China, and also to our land and sea checkpoints.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As an additional precaution, and because not all who are infected will show symptoms, we deployed healthcare teams at the aerobridge for all incoming flights from China to identify and pull aside passengers who look unwell.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, it helped that China had moved swiftly to impose restrictions on its own outbound travellers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of these measures helped to reduce the flow of people from China to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite these measures, we recognised that there was still a flow of travellers coming in from China on a regular basis.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We monitored this flow carefully and considered what additional actions were needed based on the evidence and risks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But shortly after that, the situation changed again.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As part of these travel restrictions, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) is no longer issuing new visas to those with PRC passports and suspending all such visas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is because the vast majority of such travellers coming in for short visits would have been in China recently.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But if there are PRC passport holders who have not been in China in the past 14 days, then ICA will be prepared to issue them a short-term visitor pass or to extend their short-term pass.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why I had emphasised earlier that the travel restrictions are not tied to nationality but are meant to restrict all travellers with recent travel history in China.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is necessary to reduce the flow of people coming from the source of the virus outbreak and to limit the number of imported cases coming into Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is our first line of defence at the border.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond border controls, our second line of defence is to identify and isolate the people with the virus, as well as all of the close contacts of the infected persons.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have a well-established contact tracing procedure, which we put in place during SARS, and have continued to finetune through emergency exercises and through experiences dealing with previous outbreaks like MERS and H1N1.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All of the outstanding suspect cases have been isolated.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The close contacts of the confirmed cases are also now on quarantine.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In addition, we have been contacting the recent travellers from Hubei who are presently in Singapore and putting those of higher risk on quarantine.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Persons under Quarantine are required to stay in their designated location at all times during the quarantine period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They cannot physically interact with others living in the same premises.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For each case, we will assess whether to quarantine the person at the GQF or to do so at the person’s home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In cases where the home is found to be suitable by MOH, then home quarantine would apply and we would use video calls, phone calls and regular spot checks to ensure that they remain in their assigned quarantined location.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are protocols that we have all worked out through SARs and finetuned over the years, as I mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Persons who do not have a suitable residence for quarantine would then be housed in GQF and there are severe penalties for non-compliance of the Quarantine Order, including fines or jail.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides quarantine for close contacts and high-risk groups, we have also taken precautionary measures for recent travellers from other parts of mainland China, outside of Hubei, as I mentioned just now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is one way to reduce their exposure when they are back and thus reduce the risk of community spread in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those on LOA are expected to remain in their residence as much as possible, minimise visitors and maintain a record of persons they come into close contact with.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They also need to minimise time spent in public places and contact with others, monitor their health and temperature daily, and avoid crowded places or social gatherings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have put out guidelines on what an LOA means just to ensure that anyone who is on LOA knows what they are expected to do.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They may resume normal duties or activities only after they have served their LOA, if they remain well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have put in place measures like the Quarantine Orders and LOA to protect Singaporeans from the spread of the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singaporeans must also do their part to cooperate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some residents, upon learning that there is a person under home quarantine or LOA in the same apartment block, have asked that this person be moved elsewhere.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also heard feedback of landlords stigmatising tenants based on their nationality, or worse, evicting PRC tenants who are taking their LOA.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I can appreciate that Singaporeans are very concerned about the well-being of themselves and their family members.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But if landlords start turning tenants away, then our overall containment efforts will be much harder and we end up in endangering ourselves and others.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we should not condone such irresponsible actions that will end up putting Singapore and Singaporeans at greater risk.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In such difficult times, we should not let our fears overwhelm us and cause us to overreact.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead let us support one another and look out for one another, so that we can all get through this together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This brings me to the third line of defence on community and individual responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will do everything we can in this fight against the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many of our officials are going beyond their usual duties to focus on this challenge.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They include our healthcare and medical personnel at the frontline; ICA officers manning the checkpoints; Police and Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) officers and Auxiliary Police screening incoming travellers and safeguarding persons under quarantine as well as the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) and the Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) officers at airport and cruise terminals; and many, many more.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The whole-of-Government officials are going all out to tackle this.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We need every Singaporean to play their part, to take all necessary precautions and to exercise individual and collective responsibility.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, employers can help by ensuring their employees who have just returned from China stay at home under LOA.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If anyone in the office is sick, employers should immediately ask them to see a doctor and stay at home to recover.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also have a responsibility, in this time of heightened alert, not to spread unverified information or false news which can cause needless panic and fear.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Unfortunately, in recent times, there have been various online posts and articles containing various falsehoods, for example, that we have run out of masks, that someone in Singapore has died from the virus, that Woodlands Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station was shut for disinfection.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are all false – fake news – and fortunately, we now have the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA) to deal with such fake news.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government has used POFMA to correct them and clarify the facts swiftly and we will continue to do so to avoid unnecessary panic and anxiety.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even as we address false information, we have stepped up our efforts to provide everyone with timely and accurate information.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We try to reach all segments of society through various platforms, including broadcast media, display panels in Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates, Government websites and social media.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have been using Gov.sg WhatsApp to provide timely updates to Singaporeans in all our official languages.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To date, more than 300,000 have signed up for the service and I encourage anyone who has not done so to subscribe and to get the latest verified information and advisories.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As the situation continues to evolve, we ask Singaporeans to continue turning to official or credible sources for accurate and up-to-date information.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We ask Singaporeans to be discerning and share only verified information.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Together, we can help prevent misinformation and falsehoods from sowing fear and causing panic in our society.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the individual level, it is also essential that all of us continue to uphold good personal hygiene, as emphasised by Minister Gan Kim Yong just now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Wash our hands regularly with soap, do not touch our face with our hands, cover our mouths when we cough or sneeze.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If you have flu-like symptoms, avoid public places and wear a mask on your way to the clinic, so that you do not risk infecting others.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we should all continue to emphasise these points to get the message across.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This now brings me to the topic of masks – face masks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To prepare for any emergency, stockpiles of essential items are critical.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the years, and learning from the experience of SARS and other crises, we have built up a stockpile of surgical and N95 masks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But no stockpile is sufficient if we do not use the supplies judiciously.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All were snapped up in a matter of hours.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But still, there were people who were not able to get access to a mask.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, with the virus spreading to countries all over the world, there is now a global scramble for masks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Producers around the world are struggling to keep pace with the demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And some places like Taiwan have even banned the export of masks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have existing contracts from various producers to replenish our stockpile.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in light of the current situation, we have to seriously consider the risks of our supply lines being disrupted.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why, firstly, we slowed the supply of masks to retailers and prioritised the masks for essential services, namely, our frontline healthcare workers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The nationwide distribution of masks was a major exercise in its own right.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We mobilised the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) and People's Association (PA) for this task and they all did a sterling job.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Within a very short turnaround time, the SAF had completed the packing of over five million masks and delivered them to our collection points.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our PA staff and grassroots organisations then took over to set up collection centres at CCs and Residents' Committee (RC) centres and to man the collection counters.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) chipped in and came up with a "maskgowhere" website, where you can just key in your postal code to get information on where and when to collect the masks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, let us all do our part to ensure the sustainability of our mask stockpile, so that our frontline healthcare workers will have the necessary supplies to carry out their work.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has been slightly over a month since the virus outbreak in China, and businesses are already feeling the impact – businesses here in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Depending on how the situation evolves, the impact to the economy can further broaden and intensify.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will, therefore, extend support and help for our companies and workers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We already provide a quarantine allowance to Singapore-based businesses to cover their employees who are quarantined, and to self-employed Singaporeans and Permanent Residents (PRs) who are in quarantine. the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) will also work closely with employers to support any affected workers and to protect their livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In addition, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) is working with the community and grassroots organisations to reach out to Singaporeans and PRs under quarantine.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will provide ComCare financial assistance and social support to those in need to tide through this difficult period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) has already announced the first set of measures for this sector, including the waiver of licence fees for hotels, travel agents and tour guides.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As I have said at the start, we need all Singaporeans to stand united in this fight against the coronavirus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a situation like this, fear is sometimes as great a threat to us as the disease itself.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must not allow such fears to paralyse our society.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must never allow our prejudices and fears to pull apart our society or foster greater division and suspicions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we did in SARS and other previous challenges over the years, let us find strength and confidence in one another – the strength to carry on with our lives and to support one another and defeat this virus together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I cited some examples of irresponsible behaviours earlier by landlords chasing out tenants on LOAs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Recently, a WhatsApp message has been going around with a list of places to avoid, completely ignoring the fact that any place exposed to a confirmed case will be thoroughly cleaned and disinfected, under supervision by the National Environment Agency (NEA).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But, still, a list of places to avoid is spread, and that creates fear and a perception that people should avoid these places.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Online, you can see posts directed against PRC nationals.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Such actions are not helpful and they have no place in our society.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are bigger than this in Singapore and I hope all of us here in this House, regardless of political party, and every Singaporean will stand together and we will all do our part to confront and condemn such prejudice and discrimination wherever they exist.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I am glad that these behaviours are still in the minority.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are not representative of the vast majority of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are many more out there who have been showing us the best of Singapore at work.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are quietly helping their fellow citizens in their own ways.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, at a recent house visit, I met a resident and asked if he had collected his masks and he replied that he did not need them and asked for his package of masks to be given to others who are in greater need of them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am sure many Members here would have encountered similar residents giving such feedback.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the weekend, too, we have seen residents who have spontaneously stepped forward, volunteering either by themselves or even with their children alongside them, to man the mask collection points as well as to distribute the masks to the homes of their more vulnerable neighbours, especially those with mobility issues.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Singaporeans are also doing their part through many selfless acts to support those who are affected.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Nanyang Technological University (NTU), the students are helping their friends on LOA by delivering food three times a day to them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On top of the food, they are helping to pack and deliver welfare packs, including items like snacks and hot drinks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most of all, we see Singaporeans from all walks of life carrying on with their lives with courage and calmness.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In every sector, our friends from the media are busy covering the news.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am seeing them almost every day these days and you see them busy on the ground, correspondents still in China covering the news, providing us with up-to-date information so that we are familiar with the facts and the latest developments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our frontline workers, those in our healthcare institutions, our healthcare workers, workers at our checkpoints and our airports, our transport workers, all carrying on with their lives quietly, doing whatever they can to fight this virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I want to thank everyone for showing that Singaporeans can rise to this occasion and overcoming this challenging situation together.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is the Singapore Spirit which will enable us to prevail against the virus.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At this point, no one can tell for sure how the situation will develop or how long this will last.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I am confident that we will succeed in this fight, if we stand united as an effective Government, a cohesive people and a resolute nation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: First, could the Task Force update us on how many Singaporeans remain in China?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And if there are any confirmed cases of Singaporeans remaining in China but outside of Hubei who may have contracted novel coronavirus, are there any plans for further evacuations from China?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My second question relates to the state of the economy.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While Minister Lawrence Wong has indicated that the Deputy Prime Minister will announce a slew of measures in the Budget Statement, however, can the Government provide an update at the moment of the scale of the impact on our economy so far and also the possible total impact for the coming financial year?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And if the situation worsens, what can small and medium enterprises (SMEs) do, especially businesses which are affected at the moment by supply from China as well as their workers still being in China?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What can they do in the short term?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Most of them have spouses who may not be Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, they have either chosen to remain in China for the time being or they would like to come back but we have to work out arrangements because it is not so straightforward, being married to non-Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we are still in touch with the Chinese authorities to see what else can be done for the group of people who wish to come back, and we are also in touch with the Singaporeans directly.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the scale of the impact on the economy, we are monitoring this very carefully.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think we are only seeing the initial brunt of it now because, with the viral situation continuing to grow, with the travel restrictions and the situation continuing to escalate, I am sure the impact will not only be for the sectors that are directly impacted, like trade, transport and tourism, but there will be knock-on impacts.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: China's own economy will slow down and the global economy will slow down.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: STB has already put up one set of initiatives and we are in the midst of studying if more can be done.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: First: what would his comments be for those employees who seek certification on being free from the novel coronavirus in order to go back to work?

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Second: is there a shortage of ambulance services right now because, lately, GPs have had to wait many hours for such services for emergency and novel coronavirus suspected cases?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I can expect her to raise very important questions like these.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The reason is because we test the patient based on his viral load and there is an incubation period during which the patient may have very low or zero viral load.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But at the same time, because it is the incubation period, the virus may emerge later on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, at any point in time, when we test a person, when it is negative, it does not mean that he is virus-free.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We can only say that, for this moment in time, the test shows no virus detectable in his bloodstream.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But the virus can emerge the following hour or the following day.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I have explained, first, it is not possible for such certification to be issued; second, you are simply loading our hospitals unnecessarily.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, the best way to do it is to monitor yourself if you have been exposed to contacts, or, if you have come back from China, monitor your own health for 14 days.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If there are any symptoms, wear a mask as you go to see a doctor and tell the doctor your travel history, that you have been to Wuhan or you have been to China, so that all these factors can be taken into account when we assess the patient.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But please do not go to the hospital to ask for blood tests in order to get a certificate that you are free from coronavirus.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And these ambulances are used to convey those who are suspected cases because we want to make sure that they are protected and isolated while we are transporting them to hospital for testing.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In the initial first few days, there were some organisational difficulties among the service operators.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have sat down and discussed with them and the logistics are managed better now.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Sometimes, when there is a peak, it may take a while, few minutes, an hour, but we try to respond as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have also set up a hotline for the doctors to call.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is operated by our College of Family Physicians that we help to answer queries, whether it is ambulance or any other thing.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we do recognise that, in the initial days, we do have some logistics difficulties in organising our ambulance responses.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And every time we change our case definition, it is also quite natural that it will suddenly have a larger number of suspected cases because, when you change the definition, the definition will include a bigger catchment and, therefore, we will need to adjust our logistics support accordingly.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And for our own healthcare workers and professionals, do they have sufficient rest and enough social and emotional support for their own well-being?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The third question is: are we able to activate volunteer healthcare workers to pitch in if and when the need arises?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If it is related to the topic, please feel free to surface.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Are there any specific or additional measures in schools, particularly for preschoolers and primary school children who may not always be aware or practise proper personal hygiene as we try to educate Singaporeans in this?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: And will there be a postponement or review of overseas school tours or trips seeing that there are other similar virus outbreaks beyond the 2019 novel coronavirus, for example, the avian flu or H5N1 virus outbreak in Hunan, China as well as in Chhattisgarh, India?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the manpower requirements, yes, in fact, there is a heightened need for manpower because of the intensity that we are going through – testing of the cases, quarantining them and managing them; and the management is quite intensive as you can imagine.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We also need to look after the suspect cases to detect signs of infection when they occur.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We require a lot of manpower and the rest of healthcare needs need to continue to be met.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we have been working with our clusters to ensure that there is sufficient manpower and to make sure that their schedules are also properly looked at.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We do have contingency plans in place to ensure that we have sufficient manpower to cater to situations like these.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In terms of volunteer manpower, yes, this is also part of the plan for our clusters, our hospitals to call back some of the volunteers.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some of those who are on leave also volunteered to come back and have said, "Why not I come back and help to supplement the manpower?" So, I think, all these are in place and, as we go along, we will continue to augment our manpower resources.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But at the same time, part of the plan is to see how we can reorganise ourselves into an emergency crisis mode, an outbreak mode, so that we can operate differently.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We may manage them in a different way so as to lighten the load on our core medical manpower.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: All this is part and parcel of our contingency plans.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On preschools and schools, over the weekend, educators have worked really hard.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They have developed a package, a syllabus, to teach students about what the viruses are, how they are transmitted and what we can do about it to prevent transmission.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The lessons covered are what both Minister Gan Kim Yong and Minister Lawrence Wong have described just now on how it transmits.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Therefore, two things you need to do, which is that you need to wash your hands with soap and not touch your face.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When you think about it, it becomes very hard to do.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When you do not think about it, I think it is easier.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Stop thinking about "I should not touch my face" or you will keep touching it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We want to tell students that in this fight with the nCoV virus, we are going to fight it with our hands – by washing them regularly and keeping them away from our face.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The intention is also to give the students some homework to bring home and tell their parents.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Likewise, we want to do it in preschools as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Yes, there are cases sprouting up in other parts of the world.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have to look at the facts and make the decisions decisively.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, likewise these are things that we will continue to monitor.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Indeed, fear is a greater threat to us in such a time as this.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are residents currently living near the Government quarantine facilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And they have expressed concerns about being near the folks who are asked to stay in these centres.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: If things should get worse, there could be more quarantine facilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Can I seek the Minister's views and assurance that the residents need not be fearful of any spread from these centres, even as we all believe that we are all in this together?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My second question is for the Minister for Education.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We know the mask is not effective for everything and hygiene is most effective.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Currently, most of the masks found in the marketplace and distributed are adult-sized.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are parents and staff in schools who are concerned that should there be a need, is there a supply of masks of smaller sizes?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Because some of the masks are so big, they cover the whole face of the children.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I will ask Minister Lawrence Wong to answer the question on the quarantine facilities.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On the masks, it is a more general question for children's masks.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As we mentioned or explained multiple times, the mask is to protect the person not wearing the mask.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, the mask is to prevent the cough and sneezes from the person who is sick.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, for that purpose, for younger children, the mask can be used because it is just preventing them from spitting out their sputums or their sneezes, to prevent the droplets from going out.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: With some adjustments, the masks can be used for younger children.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And if they really cannot be used, then what you should do is to use a handkerchief or whatever to cover the mouth to prevent it from spitting out and to observe hygiene.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you do that, please wash your hands.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you have to go to the hospital or clinic to see a doctor, you can use a mask.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If the child is sick and if there is no need to go out, please do not take him out.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Keep him at home so that he can rest and recover as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan asked me to read this.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: He said while I was giving my speech, he had observed that 13 out of 41 Members of Parliament sitting opposite us touching their faces within the 25 minutes.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, touching face is not easy to avoid, but please wash your hands.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it was not just Dr Intan Mokhtar, I just wanted to clarify.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Between then and now, another 13 would have done it.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, please just observe personal hygiene, wash your hands regularly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That will protect yourself and protect many people.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will only take Questions from those who do not touch their face.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They have been exposed so they are of some risk.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Number two, when they are in quarantine, there are strict protocols and procedures to ensure that they stick to, and they remain within the place of quarantine.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I mentioned a few things that we do – phone calls, video calls, spot checks, a whole range of things for home quarantine.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the quarantine facilities, there are also strict parameters.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These people will be within the location where they are quarantined.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They will not be able to wonder about so easily.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Thirdly, there are also some fears that, let us say, there is a person nearby under quarantine.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Yes, quarantine is safe, but if there is some chance that this person later on is found to be infected, then he may have moved around; then there is fear somehow that I mentioned on WhatsApp, avoid coming to this place.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With all these measures in place, we should continue to assure Singaporeans there is no need to be fearful or to overreact due to fear or panic.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If that were to happen, we do need quarantine facilities and Singaporeans all have to cooperate and we seek their understanding that this is an essential part of ensuring that we can get through the situation together.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The reason I am asking this is I have a resident who came back from Wuhan but through another airport and he is currently under home quarantine with his family.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: He told me that it was a very stressful experience for him and his family at the airport because he and his family with young children were basically kept in a locked room for about four hours waiting for vehicles to arrive to bring them back and so on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I wonder if the Minister could elaborate about what Singaporeans coming back through the airport, through the Chinese routes can expect, whether the processing time of four hours, for example, is normal or has it been more streamlined?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And whether passengers coming from Hubei and other airports are treated differently?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And, therefore, anyone coming back, we would want them to be isolated and quarantined.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Can we improve them, can we make the waiting time shorter?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am sure the agencies are going all out to see how it can be streamlined and improved.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we hope Singaporeans and travellers in this category would understand.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First of all, for new arrivals we have already stopped the flow.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But Singaporeans, PRs and long-term pass holders can still come back.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And if you are coming back from Hubei, you are of a higher risk, and we would want you to be isolated and quarantined.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But please bear with us while we work through the process and see if these processes can be continued to be improved.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That may be of some concern to the self-employed.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, perhaps we can consider some calibrated support for this group of self-employed individuals who may be on LOAs.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But let us see how we can help them tide through this period.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Speaker, the first death outside of China was reported in the Philippines.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I just want to ask for an update from the Minister on the 18 patients who are currently under observation, what is their health situation?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: And in Thailand, the doctors have apparently come up with a cure, an antidote for the virus.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: What hopes can we have on such a cure being found?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Some are saying that there are no cure virus and so on.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: So, perhaps the Minister can share on that.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: The next supplementary question, xenophobic tendency and sentiments have surfaced around the world.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In Singapore's context, we are a small country, how can we safeguard ourselves from having such a tendency in the public?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I will deal with the first two questions and leave it to Minister Lawrence Wong to deal with the last question.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: First, on the status of the 18 confirmed cases, I gave an update in my speech earlier.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But that is something that we are working towards.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will continue to provide them with support.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That means, we are not able to definitively cure a person.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There will be news of possible discoveries because scientists are working overtime to make sure to put in efforts to discover ways to contain the virus and treat the virus and also to prevent the virus through vaccines.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I think vaccines and curative treatment are being looked into.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But I think it will take time to develop the method and to also test the treatment to make sure that they are effective and safe for patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is not going to happen overnight.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It may take quite a while before we see a curative treatment being determined.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: During this period, it is better for us to focus on how we can manage, contain the spread and put in the necessary measures to protect our population.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Member said anti-PRC sentiments are showing up everywhere in the world arising from this virus outbreak.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And as I mentioned in my speech just now, we see this in Singapore, too.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I mentioned just now, all of us should take a united stand to condemn such prejudices or discriminatory behaviours or actions whenever we see them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It can have repercussions on our whole containment efforts and can be ultimately harmful to all of us.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, for specific actions, we will look at them and engage the landlord and see if tougher action needs to be taken.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But for the overall tone of society, we need everyone to speak up, to voice up and we need every Singaporean to do their part to condemn such behaviour.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, they, too, see the need and recognise the need for travel restrictions on its own people and to contain the virus in China.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, what we and many other countries that have put in place similar restrictions are doing, are really complementary to China's own actions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is in all of our interest, be it China, Singapore or any other country.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is in our collective interest to tackle this situation together as a global community in order to limit the spread of the virus and contain it as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Such solutions aid Singaporeans, the region and the wider community of nations.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I could not quite get the first question.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The first step is to better understand the virus and how it evolves and how it behaves so that we can then develop appropriate vaccines.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There is already ongoing collaboration and we continue to explore opportunities.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These collaborations are between our research institutions as well as companies which are involved in some of these development of vaccines.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: WHO and the various international organisations also provide platforms for sharing of knowledge and information.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This area is quite vibrant and we have quite a few entities that are involved.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some of them, of course, involve commercial undertaking and, therefore, there will be some commercial sensitivity as well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There are avenues for this to continue and we want to also encourage more collaboration globally.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The second question is: what are the protocols involved in a community spread?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It depends on the different types of community spread.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The first possibility is a very limited community spread, meaning it could spread from person A to person B, and then person B passes it on to person C.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, person C has no direct relationship to person A.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is also a form of community transmission but this transmission is likely to then be quite limited to one or two generations.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If we are able to react quickly, able to contain patient C and patient B, then we will be able to contain the spread.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, if patient C is a contact of patient B, and we are able to trace patient C once we identified patient B, even it has been transmitted to patient C, then we are still able to say that patient C is probably contained.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In such a situation, you may then need to assess what is the landscape at that time, what are the risks that are involved.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I mentioned in my speech, we may have to begin to look at how we can reduce or restrict human-to-human interaction.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But exactly which steps we are going to introduce will depend on the exact nature of the community spread.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have a framework of various options that are available and each of them will be deployed depending on the situation prevailing at that point in time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: One of the roles or duties of the task force is to make an assessment as the situation evolves and decide what are the appropriate measures to introduce when the time comes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just two supplementary questions, I believe, for Minister Lawrence Wong.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first one is, there is, of course, a Price Control Act (PCA) and there were reports of traders of masks who were profiteering, charging very high prices.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I understand that the Price Controller has written to some of them.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And, of course, as economists all know, using price controls has its downside and its risks.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
