text: My second supplementary question is with regard to the method of distribution of masks.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There could be some advantages to mailing out masks in terms of not encouraging people to cluster together and so on.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe that there was an exercise in 2014 when some organisations mailed out N95 masks during the haze period.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I just wanted to understand the thinking a bit more and whether mailing out of masks is something that might be done in future, if such cases arise.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will not rule out any option at this stage.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Price Controller is pursuing, investigating, getting more information and, if need be, more actions can be taken.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But, as of now, I would say, looking at the prices, some of these platform providers have cooperated.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I heard recently that some of them have even removed some of these listings with very exorbitant prices.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, anyway, the Price Controller is on top of this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is following up on the matter and it will consider actions that need to be taken against profiteering.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Like I have mentioned earlier, even in the collection exercise, when we go around and residents come to us, they say, "Actually, please, I do not need the masks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is proceeding in a very orderly fashion.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If you go to any of these collection centres now, there are no queues.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are designated times to pick up the masks so there are no large crowds at all in any of them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: People are just picking up as and when they are free during the designated times.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, based on the exercise that we have done so far, I would say this distribution method is more effective.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: He mentioned that if there is widespread community spread, we may have to close the schools and I suppose even the preschools.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But there are actually families where both parents are working and it is very difficult for them to take time off to look after the kids and we do not know how long this will last.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, when we announce any school closure, will we also announce what are the alternatives that will be available to these parents?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think Minister Gan Kim Yong is doing the right thing to paint future scenarios that are possible that we should be prepared for, so it is not as if we are going to do it straightaway.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But it is something we have to consider, to prepare plans taking into account the considerations that Mr Yee Chia Hsing has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Bear in mind that when SARS was at its height, we did suspend schools for a couple of weeks.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If it comes to that, if we have do it, we have to do it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we will have to look at the data, look at the evidence, look at the situation and take into account all considerations before making any decisions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The question from Mr Yee Chia Hsing highlights an important point, that for every measure that we contemplate about introducing, there will always be an impact on the society.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And therefore, we have to evaluate and assess every measure very carefully, taking into account the impact on society, as I have mentioned in my speech.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: None of the decisions or measures is easy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are always weighing the pros and cons and, eventually, we have to decide what makes sense for us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I would assure Mr Yee that when we make a decision, whether it is school suspension or any other decision, we will always take into account the impact on individuals, on the society, on different groups of people.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We want to make sure that for those who are affected, we do our best to help them address their concerns and their problems.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: My question is: in the event if we need to step up to using N95 masks because there is wide community spread or for future viral outbreaks, how do you ensure that the public are fitted with the right model of N95 masks?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Because what is being done in the healthcare institutions is we actually go for mask fitting test to ensure that there is optimal protection, because different models fit different face shapes and the public may not be aware of this.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: N95 masks are generally used by the healthcare professionals.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In fact, we have kept telling people that you do not need the mask for the haze.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Anyway, people still wear them for the haze.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, as Ms Irene Quay has mentioned, if you do not fit it properly, the mask really does not protect you.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If need be, we will carry out the necessary education to reach out to Singaporeans to explain to them how to protect themselves.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think to teach each of them how to wear the N95 mask to be as effective as in the healthcare environment is going to be quite difficult and you may end up giving them a false sense of security.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And as a result, you may end up with more infections, which is counterproductive.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I would say that the N95 mask is not going to be the main focus for outbreak control, if there is extensive community transmission.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have a question for Minister Gan Kim Yong.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I read with concern the reports of infection of healthcare workers in China today.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: During SARS, we, too, had doctors and nurses working with infected patients getting infected themselves.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, in today's context, can the Minister share what measures are taken today to better protect our healthcare workers, especially those on the frontline taking care of the patients who are infected?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Despite the best protection, in some cases, healthcare workers are infected.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In cases like in China, for example, and very often, this happens at the initial stage of the outbreak because healthcare workers are unfamiliar with the virus, they may not understand that it is infectious or it is as infectious as we are seeing, so, therefore, the precautions may not be adequate.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As time progresses, when we get to know the virus better, the protection measures will be enhanced.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For us in Singapore, we have stepped up our protective measures and particularly because we have gone through the experience of SARS and several other disease outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are very painful lessons in our memory and, therefore, our healthcare institutions have exercised extra caution when they deal with these infected patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our healthcare workers and our healthcare institutions are very mindful of the risks that are involved.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our frontline workers, those who are in the Emergency Department, our GPs, they are also very alert to the potential risks.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If they have potential risk of contamination, they will put them aside, give them a mask to wear so that they do not contaminate others.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are the practices that have been put in place.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But whatever precautionary measures we have put in place, we must be very mindful and be very cautious.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If we are careless, none of these measures will help us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we constantly remind our healthcare workers to remember to be cautious, to protect themselves and, at the same time, protect the patients.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Seventeen years later, I am still involved in managing patients at the frontline with this coronavirus outbreak.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I have to say that we have been working with MOH over the years and I would like to applaud MOH on its communications, coordination and also performance now, 17 years down the line.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I have to say that we are performing at top-notch.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: So, thank you to all the MOH staff and also all the people who are working long hours behind the scenes.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: One of the things that has been very, very useful for us is the MOH surveillance hotline, which operates 24 hours.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I am able to call them 24 hours, anytime, to check on locations as well as quarantine orders and any other information.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I hope that MOH can continue with this for as long as we need it, even beyond that.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The second point is essentially about publicity and also perhaps education for people who are coming forward.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: We have got employers who are saying that these two air-con repairmen have gone to the room where there was a suspected case.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: They are asymptomatic but the employers have asked them to come to the Emergency Department of a tertiary hospital to be assessed.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Of course, we will assess and send them away to the GPs because we do not want to overload the hospital.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Perhaps we can do more education for people like these.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: We understand the concerns and the worry that the public may have and people who may have been so-called spinoffs or been associated in some indirect way with people who may have been suspected of having the infection.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But perhaps more publicity and education, and perhaps working with the media as well, will help.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: One of his main jobs is to look at public education, to share with Singaporeans more information and timely information so that they are better prepared.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Things like fake news or wrong information ought to be clarified so that they know exactly what to do, rather than to be misled.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I have mentioned earlier on, there is actually no way to certify a person fit for work and free of the virus.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: He has to go through the incubation period to make sure that he does not have symptoms, then he can go back to work.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, if you are in doubt, you have been exposed, the best is to exercise precaution, exercise self-discipline, be socially responsible and make sure you wash your hands very regularly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is the best way to protect yourself and your loved ones.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Whenever in doubt, whenever there is a suspected case or a confirmed case, we will advise the premises on how to clean it.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Practices are in place, protocols are in place, but the Member is right that we need to educate the general public so that they understand that these places are rendered safe and secure, and there is no need to stay away from these places.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: You can see the list getting longer and longer, because we do expect to see suspected cases emerging from time to time, going forward.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Even though we have travel controls, we will continue to see suspected cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For each suspected case, we will need to ensure that our medical staff wear all the protective gear, because they are by nature suspected cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Many of the suspected cases turn out to be negative and, therefore, if you see some of our healthcare colleagues donning PPE at your shopping centre and so on, do not assume that this is going to be a confirmed case, because it may just be precautions that they have taken to inspect and pick up the suspected cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Eventually, it may turn out to be a negative case.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The best is to exercise self-discipline, be socially responsible, make sure that you observe basic hygiene practices.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think that is the best way to protect yourself.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The first one is: what are we doing to encourage employers to be generous with respect to paid medical leave, paid family leave for workers who are sick, who may need to self-isolate, who may need to take care of a close family member who is sick?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I am asking this because I stand corrected, but I am not sure right now that paid leave is actually mandated for self-isolation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We would not want employers to ask employees to take their own annual leave or no pay leave in such cases.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The second question is: Mr Ang Hin Kee has already spoken about the financial constraints faced by self-employed persons who have to go on LOA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But I think the problem goes beyond that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Because even when self-employed persons have to go see the doctor or just take a day off work because they are not feeling well, they do not earn any income.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I think this is another area where we can look into providing wage support, maybe medical cost support, because again, we do not want to be counterproductive here.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We do not want people to have to choose between taking care of their health and earning a livelihood.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I think the Member's question also extends to persons who are not required to be on LOA, but either as their own unilateral sense that they should stay away, because they are not feeling well, or they have to look after someone who is on LOA.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In those instances, I think we have to allow the employer to exercise some flexibility.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If it is a situation where the employer has come into agreement with this individual, well and good.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I think the employers know what to do.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But there is really no requirement for a person to stay away from work if they themselves are not being asked to fulfil an LOA requirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is only something that they are doing on top of, so I just wanted to be clear on that.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I just want to echo and express my thanks to Minister Gan Kim Yong for his statement of thanks and support for healthcare workers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Two short but slightly technical questions, I apologise.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The first, the Minister touched about it earlier.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think many Singaporeans are looking forward to the day when the first of the novel coronavirus patients are discharged from hospital.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could I just ask what are the criteria for discharge?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Because there does not seem to be an international consensus on it, as far as I know.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One of the key hallmarks of the SARS virus was that there existed these subsets of patients known as "super spreaders".

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, if you look at this novel coronavirus, the ratio of transmission as we reported, about 2.2, which is, on the average, one will pass to about 2.2 persons.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: SARS was much lower, but then there are these "super spreaders" which caused a havoc in our healthcare sector.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I was just wondering whether there is any information coming up from anywhere whether there exists such "super spreaders".

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Dr Chia knows I am not a doctor, so I can only do what I can as a Minister for Health.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We can leave it in their hands to make a professional judgement when is the appropriate time to discharge patient.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And, Ministers, I must assure you, do not interfere in their discharge proceedings because it is purely professional judgement.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu is right that we are all looking out for the risk of a "super spreader" emerging.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is where one particular patient may infect tens or hundreds of patients that come into contact with him and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are potential multipliers that will cause a major outbreak in the premises, in the locality.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It may happen but it is not yet being detected.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But we are all looking out for them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Sometimes, the "super spreaders", the patients themselves, may be quite well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, he is able to go around many places and spread a lot of potential contamination in the environment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, it is something that we are looking out for.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu is right that this would be a problem if this occurs in Singapore, China or anywhere else, so it is something that we will continue to monitor.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister is there any way to monitor, to ensure that they comply to the 14 days of LOA strictly?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question is, for those who are returning and due to whatever reason they have no place to go back to, is there any help that is given or will be given to them?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Just to give an example, I received an email from my resident.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But her husband does not want her to return to their home because the employer of the husband has imposed this rule that if any of your family members comes back from China, you have to stay at home as well.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: That is the reason the husband does not want the wife.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Because Hong Kong is very near China and there is some concern among residents as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Hong Kong has fewer confirmed cases than Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Maybe people might want to apply travel restrictions on Singapore then.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think our approach is to be looking at evidence, at the source of where the virus is, how widely it is spreading and which are the at-risk sources.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Yes, I think we will not rule out more actions on travel restrictions, as we have said, but it has to be based not just on geographical proximity or distance but based on evidence on the nature of the virus, how widely it is spreading, at the risk.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And if there are risks posed to Singapore and Singaporeans, we will not rule out other measures on travel restrictions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That exercise is underway now, so that we can be ready when these workers return, be ready to engage the employers, to be ready to engage the landlords.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If some of them are living in dorms, be ready to ensure that our dorms are properly fitted out to have these workers living in more isolated areas without interaction and contamination with their fellow workers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is the work that is happening, already been happening and we are continuing with this process.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The question is what happens if employers need help because they say they are impacted by their workers who are coming back and unable to work, what happens if family members need help because somebody is on LOA within their home and then they, too, are impacted.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think these are all questions that we are anticipating.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is all part of the package of measures we are looking at to help companies, employers and households as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will, as I said earlier, put in place a series of measures to help those who are impacted and we will take all this into consideration in our package.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: F-E-A-R is also false evidence appearing real so I am going to ask Minister Gan Kim Yong if I can go straight to the source of fear, which is the fear of death.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Could he explain to us how death occurs from this virus?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Because there is this panic and hysteria that the moment we "kena", we are just going to drop dead.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: So, it would be really useful if we can explain how death occurs from one who actually gets infected.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: What I understand is that most of the death cases right now from China have occurred in people who are elderly and who are at risk.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: It would be really helpful for us to know how the virus impacts us physically and that could lead to death.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The second question I have is looking at the Fear Factor that impacts the economy and employment.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: There have been a lot of companies that are cancelling commercial activities and projects and events.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I am wondering if the Government or the Ministry of Trade and Industry perhaps think that there may be merit to issue clear guidelines to companies in terms of cancellation or postponement of commercial activities and business events, because there is definitely a knock-on effect on small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and social enterprises.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Also, now that I know from Minister Gan Kim Yong that the virus is not airborne, I really would encourage all of us to take three deep breaths every time, every day, as we calm our minds and heart.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is very difficult for me to describe the process of death in medical terms, but I would try to explain how it causes death.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is important for us to ensure that we continue to stay healthy.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, what the hospitals will do is to provide supportive care to ensure that you have time for your body to recover, for your body to be able to fight the virus on its own until we are able to develop a definitive curative treatment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think that is how the process will happen.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Member is right, generally, coronavirus affect patients who have underlying conditions more, and, generally, the older people tend to have more underlying conditions and, therefore, they tend to affect the older people more.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But there are also exceptions and even in this novel coronavirus situation, we see that there were some in their 30s and 40s who are also infected, and some may not have underlying conditions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the end, it is also an issue of statistics.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When you have a large enough number of people who died, at the end of the day, there will be some who are not so typical, who not necessarily have conditions, but they have more severe reactions for a variety of reasons.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But generally, coronavirus affects people with underlying conditions mainly because your organs tend to fail progressively as the disease progresses.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The second question is on the impact on our economy and can we provide clear guidelines on major events.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Yes, cancellations of events are rampant right now; and these are even business and commercial activities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Events can continue but organisers take extra precautions.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, there is no need for cancellations; continue with the events.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if it is a large-scale event, then you might want to take precautions like having temperature screenings, which I think many event organisers are doing, and then putting out advisories to remind the participants that if they are sick, do not show up.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If they have been to China recently, then make sure that they stay at home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those sorts of precautions are useful, and we continue to remind companies and event organisations of these precautions.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The official communication channel to the people who subscribe to the WhatsApp group quoted the Prime Minister saying that "Experts think that the Wuhan virus may be less deadlier than SARS".

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But as I have said, it is still at the early stage of the development of the disease, the numbers will change over time.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In fact, as more and more milder cases are detected, the denominator may tend to go up and, therefore, the number may come down.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the same time, those who are confirmed cases today and, progressively, they may die because of the progression of the disease.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Our hearts and our prayers go to those Singaporeans who are still in Wuhan.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: When we heard that the 92 Singaporeans are brought back to Singapore, we were very happy to hear that.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The second part is that it is in times like this that we see the best of humans and we see the worst of humans.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: In the last two days, when we go around doing the mask distribution, we see a lot of encouraging signs.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We see volunteers coming down to help at the mask distribution point.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We see residents coming down to give drinks, give food to the volunteers.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I have a lot of new volunteers suddenly joining in to say that they want to do their part.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I also have an ex-grassroots leader whose both legs were amputated and as a result he cannot serve as a grassroots leader anymore because of diabetes.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I hope that the Government and MFA would work harder now to see how we can bring them back.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have spoken personally to the Chinese Foreign Minister and I can assure Members, based on our conversation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My next point is that I want to make an appeal to all Singaporeans who are in China to e-register with MFA.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This enables us to stay in close touch with them to monitor their condition, to give them appropriate advice, recommendations and, obviously, if there is a possibility or a need to mount further operations, this ability to communicate quickly and effectively is absolutely necessary.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If they did, it would have been contravening not only their own regulations but also WHO recommendations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If additional support is needed, obviously, we will look at that.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And that also brings to mind what Minister Gan Kim Yong said just now that this problem is not just a Chinese problem, it is not just China's problem.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is a common threat confronting all of us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This virus does not respect passports or nationalities, race or language.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Member has cited an example of volunteers.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is the time when you will see the best, and sometimes, you will see the worst in humanity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I am confident that because of what we have been through 17 years ago – I recall that personally – I am confident Singaporeans will demonstrate the best of humanity and we will get through this and we will get through this together.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, rest assured, all the Singaporeans who are overseas – MFA – we will not leave anyone behind, we will look out for you.
